_doc: Nagpur (NMC) upstream sources for Headwaters. Every artifact Nagpur ships names its upstreams by id, with the artifact in that id's dependsOn.

Order: supply (NMC Environment Status Report and budget, the MWRRA order on NMC's Pench water), reservoirs (the Pravah dam bulletin read for the Nagpur district block, and its dated Marathi archive), groundwater (NWDP telemetry), rivers (MPCB monthly polluted-stretch readings, NMC's river and STP tables, MPCB station list and progress reports), geography (NMC GIS outline and zones, MRSAC ward, water-body and drainage layers, the final ward notification), flood (IMD cell and observatory tables, Maharain circle gauges, the City Development Plan 2041), commitments and lakes (Government Resolutions, AMRUT 2.0, the court docket, NMC decks, JICA and ADB documents, the Smart City list, the gazetteers and CWC's dam register), story and civic copy (the Origins sources, the disaster plans, Orange City Water, Wikimedia Commons).

Maharashtra-wide and platform upstreams stay under their existing ids and carry Nagpur's paths in their dependsOn rather than being duplicated: IN-GRES (ingres-groundwater-maharashtra, pune.json); the WRD Government Resolutions (mahagr-wrd-resolutions), the WRD flood-line register (wrd-flood-line-maps), MPCB water-quality reports (mpcb-water-quality-reports) and the CWC reservoir bulletin (cwc-reservoir-bulletin-archive) in mumbai.json; CPCB NWMP (cpcb-nwmp, surat.json); OpenStreetMap, IMD gridded rain, Open-Meteo, FABDEM and the CPCB polluted-stretch report in platform.json. The Pravah bulletin is registered per city (mumbai.json wrd-pravah-dam-feed, pune.json wrd-pravah-pune-dams, wrd-pravah-nagpur-dams here) because scrape_pravah_dams.py names one source id per city in each artifact's envelope.

nmc-esr-river-stp-tables watches the same report as nmc-esr on purpose: the river and STP tables are refreshed by a different producer with different traps, so a new edition raises one actionable alert per producer.

wrd-pravah-nagpur-dams carries no ciBlocked field on purpose. mwrdpravah.in does not answer GitHub runners, but the entry is detection 'continuous', which the edition checker never fetches; a ciBlocked flag would make CI report it CHECK-FAILED every week. The runner block is recorded in refreshMethod and notes instead, as on the Mumbai and Pune entries.

Neither MRSAC's nor NMC's ArcGIS service states a licence (copyrightText empty, no terms page). Both are state and municipal publications cited with attribution; the absence of stated terms is recorded in each entry's notes, not in the licence string.

Five GRs cited by the commitments register were read from the orgpedia mahGRs archive copy because the official PDF path answered 404 on 15 Oct 2026 (both the Marathi and English folders): 202211021115299425 (Naik lake), 202211021157345625 (Lendi lake), 202303061239587125 (AMRUT 2.0 water supply), 202304061347581325 (AMRUT 1.0 pipeline replacement) and 202304201803571027 (Kolar-Kanhan barrage, WRD). Re-try the official path at each review; the register labels these rows.

The story and the civic copy (ACTIONS_BY_CITY.nagpur helplines, the nagpur lines in src/content/my-ward/sources.ts) are hand-written content with page citations in the file headers, not generated artifacts: refreshing means re-reading the cited page and editing the prose or the card, never a script.

playbook: Table 6.2's monthly 'pure water supply' rows are the SUPPLIED total (257.642 Mcum in 2023-24, 704 MLD over 366 days). The text's '410 MLD (pure water supply of 257.642 MCM)' invites calling 257.642 the billed volume; it is not. 410 MLD billed is about 150 Mcum a year.

The loss percentage is NMC's own figure. Recompute it from billed over supplied and carry both when they differ: 2023-24 prints 41.91% (410 of 706 gives 41.93%); 2022-23 prints 47% while its own table gives 45%.
Table 6.2 need not close: in 2022-23 the twelve rows add to 250.672 against a printed 250.679. The producer asserts rows and gap separately; change ROWS_2022_23 only after checking the page image.

Dark zones: the ESR says 'certain areas under 36 CAs'. That is some areas within 36 command areas, never 36 whole command areas, and the ESR's word 'still' stays inside the quote. No citywide hours-of-supply figure exists in any edition.
Printed page = PDF page - 1 in 2023-24 and 2022-23. The 2017-18 draft is +13 (printed p.23 = PDF p.36).
The tanker baseline of 346 is dated 2016 by the ESRs and 2018 by the budgets. Carry both; do not reconcile.
The ESR's population figure cites macrotrends.net, not a census or NMC count. Do not adopt it.
Edition series: Pench II is 133 MLD in the 2017-18 draft and 175 MLD from 2022-23; Old Gorewada (16 MLD) is in the 2017-18 list only. Carry both lists as printed.
sources.notes: The ESR's water-supply section (s.6.2.1 in 2022-23 and 2023-24) is NMC's only published water balance: plants and capacities, supply, billed volume, loss, command areas, dark zones, tankers, AMRUT pipeline progress and point-of-use test results. 2023-24: https://nmcnagpur.gov.in/assets/300/2025/08/Public-Notices/ESR_Final_Report_2023-2024.pdf (203 pp, posted Aug 2025). 2022-23: https://www.nmcnagpur.gov.in/assets/300/2025/08/Public-Notices/ESR_final_Report_2022-2023.pdf. 2019-20: live URL 404, Wayback 20220806150918 works. The 2017-18 draft exists only on a third-party mirror (caknnagpur871784109.wordpress.com) and is the only edition with the raw-water reservation and billing table (Table 4.3). ESR 2024-25 was tabled at the NMC general body around 22 Apr 2026 according to the press but was not online on 15 Oct 2026. The public-notices page shows only recent uploads and keeps no ESR index, so a link-set watch would match nothing between editions: hence human-review. playbook: Budget 2026-27 (6a1d606eebca4_nmcbudget2026.pdf) is a Xerox scan with no text layer. OCR it (tesseract mar+eng, 200 dpi) and then read every figure again on the page image; the water section is printed pp.B-3 to B-4 = PDF pp.9-10. Record the method as 'OCR, checked on page image p.N'.
Budget 2025-26's speech pages carry Unicode text, but its account tables use the legacy Kruti Dev font that pdftotext cannot read as digits; decode those by hand.

Tankers: 'सध्या केवळ N टँकर कार्यरत' is the current count and 346 is the 2018 baseline; the stated reduction must equal 346 minus N (309 and 37 in 2026-27; 287 and 59 in 2025-26). The producer asserts it.
The speech counts '106 पाण्याच्या टाक्या' (water tanks); the ESR counts 73 command areas. Different units: never substitute one for the other.
The 2026-27 speech, dated May 2026, reports water revenue received 'जानेवारी 2027 पर्यंत'. Carry it as printed with [sic]; do not silently change the year.
Revenue lines are budget estimates and receipts to date, not audited accounts.
sources.notes: The Commissioner's budget speech is NMC's most current statement of its water network: connections, water tanks, distribution length, tankers in service, AMRUT progress and water revenue. 2026-27 (listed as 'NMC Budget 2025-26-27', 08/05/2026): https://nmcnagpur.gov.in/assets/300/2026/06/mediafiles/6a1d606eebca4_nmcbudget2026.pdf, 340 pp. 2025-26 (listed as 'NMC Budget 2024-25-26', 05/06/2025): https://nmcnagpur.gov.in/assets/300/2025/06/mediafiles/Final_budget_2024-_2025-2026_(1).pdf, 295 pp. The speech gives no supply volume, loss, per-capita or hours figure. The fund statement in Budget 2025-26 (printed pp.230-231) carries a Rs 28 crore line for the cost of drawing Pench water (head A23801931111), a money figure only.

playbook: The final order (Order No. 13/2018, 12 Sep 2018, 52 pp printed 'Page n of 50') and the three interim orders are scans. OCR at 250 dpi, then check every figure on the page image.

Attribute every statement to its speaker. Paras 12-17 are the petitioner's account and print the 78 Mcum sanction as 31 Mar 1998; NMC (para 32(i)) and the Pench Project Officer (para 34(iii)) date it 21 Mar 1998. The Authority's own findings are in para 50 and its directions in para 52.
Para 50(v) prints NMC's 2017-18 quota as 139.03 Mcum, 'which includes 118.05 ... domestic and 21.01 ... industrial'; the parts add to 139.06. Carry as printed.
The order records three design utilisations for the Pench complex (965, 708 and 1,087 Mcum, para 50(v)) and directs a review (52(iii)). Do not compute a deficit-year cut from any of them.

Wrong host: mwrra.org answers 525. Orders live under https://mwrra.maharashtra.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Case-No-8-of-2017-{Final-Order,Ist-Interim-Order,2nd-Interim-Order,3rd-Interim-Order}.pdf.
This watch fires on ANY newly disposed petition. Open the new order's first page and act only if it concerns Nagpur, NMC or the Pench Project Complex.
Direction 52(vii) asked NMC for a time-bound loss-reduction programme and annual reports to the Authority, also to be put in the public domain. Look for them before calling that gap closed.
sources.notes: Case No. 8 of 2017 asked the Authority to curtail NMC's use of Pench water in favour of irrigation. The final order holds the additional 78 Mcum reservation 'legal and intact as on today' under section 31B of the MWRRA (Amendment and Continuance) Act 2011, records the 1998 sanction, its 2008 conversion to permanent on conditions (an agreement within 90 days; Rs 8,445 lakh for 8,445 ha of irrigation command) and the 2010 and 2011 steps, NMC's 2017-18 water budget (197.33 Mcum from the Pench complex), the CADA entitlement table of 10 Apr 2018 and the Chief Auditor's audit (57.64% non-revenue water, Nov 2016-Oct 2017). NMC also told the Authority that a closed pipeline replaced the 48.4 km canal from April 2015 (para 32(v)). The Authority's bulk water tariff order for 2026-29 is at https://mwrra.maharashtra.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/ and is not yet used here.

sources.refreshMethod: neer-vazhvu-api/scripts/scrape_pravah_dams.py --city nagpur --out public/data/nagpur-dam-storage.json --supabase, daily from the local scheduled job (~/.local/neervazhvu-ops/refresh-blocked-feeds.sh, 12:00 IST, the step after Pune). mwrdpravah.in does not answer GitHub runners, and .github/workflows/pravah-dam-refresh.yml must not take a third city. History: backfilled once on 18 Oct 2026 from the dated Marathi archive by neer-vazhvu-api/scripts/backfill_pravah_marathi_archive.py (see the last playbook entry); a rerun is insert-only (--dry-run first; --supabase on the owner's word).
playbook: Match the WHOLE label inside the 'Nagpur' district block of the Nagpur region, never a substring anywhere: 'Nand' and 'Wadgaon' are short and generic, and the Gondiya block has its own Dhapewada. The scraper does this for a city with a `district` key. With require_all it writes nothing if Totladoh or Kamthi Khairy (the db_filter dams) is missing; a missing context dam (Khindsi, Nand, Wadgaon) prints a WARNING and the other dams are still written to the artifact and the database.

Five rows, two of them NMC's: Totladoh -> totladoh and Kamthi Khairy -> navegaon_khairi feed NMC's Pench schemes; Khindsi (NRLD 'RAMTEK'), Nand and Wadgaon (Lower Wunna) are irrigation dams kept in the artifact for context and never written to reservoir_daily_v2 (db_filter: corporations).

No row is named 'Pench'. Three other publishers use that word for three different dams: CWC's weekly bulletin calls Totladoh 'PENCH' (older spelling 'PENCH (TOTALADOH)'), NWDP's 'Pench Dam' and 'Pench Project' sit at Kamthi Khairy's coordinates, and Madhya Pradesh's 'Pench Dam' is the Machagora structure upstream.

Storage is WHOLE-DAM live storage of a hydro-electric reservoir shared with Madhya Pradesh (Totladoh) and an irrigation dam (Kamthi Khairy). It is never NMC's share; NMC holds a reservation (190 Mcum a year in the first phase, WRD GR of 19 Mar 2020). No days-left runway is computed from it.

The percentage is of DESIGNED LIVE storage (the reservoir_daily_v2 column is called storage_pct_frl for historical reasons). The bulletin prints no FRL; Totladoh's FRL 490.00 m is from CWC's weekly bulletin, Kamthi Khairy's is not published in any source used here.

Designed (dead, live, gross) Mcum are fixed per dam: Totladoh 150.00/1016.93/1166.93, Kamthi Khairy 39.00/141.98/180.98, Khindsi 0.00/103.00/103.00, Nand 9.00/53.18/62.18, Wadgaon 16.60/134.90/151.50. They equal NRLD-2019 to the cubic metre for Totladoh (p.196) and Kamthikhairy (p.172); Nand (p.197) and Wadgaon (p.205) equal at the bulletin's 0.01 Mcum precision; Khindsi (NRLD RAMTEK p.151) matches on live storage only (NRLD gross 105.13 Mcum). The scraper warns if one changes; a resurvey means updating NAGPUR_DESIGNED, fullCapacityMcft in src/cities/nagpur/config.ts and the 061 migration together.

Never use CWC's weekly PENCH storage or percentage: its 1.091 BCM capacity is a different denominator (its own storage at FRL is 1.016 BCM, i.e. Pravah's 1,016.93 Mcum), and its storage figure stayed at 1.017 BCM (93.21 %) in every bulletin from 23.07.2026 to 08.10.2026 while the level it printed moved between 484.86 m and 481.80 m. Its level column is consistent with the state bulletin.

The header date flips at midnight and per-dam readings arrive through the morning (Kamthi Khairy 06:49 AM, Khindsi stamped 12:00 AM on 15/10/2026), so a run before about 09:00 IST can carry yesterday's values under today's header. reservoir_daily_v2 rows carry the REPORT date (newest reading); the per-dam date stays in the artifact.

MARATHI ARCHIVE. The same bulletin is kept per date at https://wrd.maharashtra.gov.in/Upload/PDF/Today%27s-Storage-ReportMarathi-DD-MM-YYYY.pdf (apostrophe URL-encoded; the English filename does not exist). Values equal the English PDF of the same day (checked 15-10-2026 for all five rows). Coverage: first copy found 25 Feb 2024 (1 Feb and 15-24 Feb 2024 return 404; 2-14 Feb not checked), with holes after it (15-03-2024 is 404). Every request takes about 50 s, a 404 included; never HEAD (it 404s), always GET. Digits are Devanagari, the time reads 'स.' for AM, and pdftotext breaks the dam names apart (vowel signs land on the neighbouring line), so match rows on the designed triple inside the नागपूर block, never on the name. Each dam row carries its own reading date (15-10-2025: Kamthi Khairy dated 14/10/2025, Totladoh 15/10/2025). The backfill stores the FILE (report) date, as the live scraper stores the report date (on the 25 files checked the file date equals the newest reading in the file); the per-dam reading date stays in the dry-run JSONL (reading_date), and a file whose newest reading is not the file date is reported.

Backfill is INSERT-ONLY: never overwrite a row the live feed wrote. A day missing from the archive stays missing; the live scraper's same-date-last-year rows are reconstructed (ly_% x live capacity) and also must not be overwritten by archive rows for the same date unless the owner decides otherwise. The reverse holds too: CITIES['nagpur']['ly_insert_only'] makes the live scraper send its same-date-last-year rows in a second upsert with ignore_duplicates, so a reading already stored for that date (live or archive) keeps its value, and a same-date-last-year row printed 0.0 is not sent (column 11 printed 0.0 for both Pench dams in the 01-04-2024 file; a real empty day then stays a gap). Today's rows are merge-upserted as before. Mumbai and Pune do not set the flag and are unchanged (byte-identical rows and calls on the 14 and 15 Oct 2026 bulletins); whether they adopt it is the owner's call.

mwrdpravah.in: TLS chain incomplete (verification off); dated URLs 404 and every date parameter on pdfLatestReportEng is ignored; the home page's 'District Wise Report' buttons return an OFBiz NullPointerException page. GitHub runners time out on the host.

Do not reach for NWDP to fill gaps: 'Reservoir Discharge, Pench Dam' is zero in every row of both files and sits at Kamthi Khairy, and the two Totladoh level datasets published 14 Oct 2026 carry an 'Other (Non-Commercial)' licence (not served, decision D14).

BACKFILL DONE 18 Oct 2026. Archive dates 15 Feb 2024 to 17 Oct 2026: 976 asked, 927 files, 49 never archived (first copy 25 Feb 2024). 1,745 Totladoh and Kamthi Khairy rows qualified and 1,743 were inserted (2 dates already held the live scraper's same-date-last-year rows), giving reservoir_daily_v2 887 Totladoh and 860 Kamthi Khairy days from 25 Feb 2024. 109 rows were NOT written because the file repeated an earlier reading for that dam (reading date before the file date; mark_rows in the script), so no reading sits under a date it was not taken on; 18 cases where a later file revised an earlier day's value keep each file's own value under its own date. A rerun over the same range inserts nothing; to extend, run --dry-run then --supabase over the new dates only.
sources.notes: Daily all-Maharashtra live-storage PDF; per-dam rows for MAJOR projects only (138 statewide on 15/10/2026), grouped Region -> District. The Nagpur district block lists exactly five: Kamthi Khairy, Khindsi, Nand, Totladoh, Wadgaon. Gorewada, Ambazari and the Kanhan intake are not in the bulletin (city config carries them as no-feed sources). A daily feed has no editions to watch - detection 'continuous'; liveness is owned by check-data-freshness.ts (one reservoir_daily_v2 check per waterSource with a public feed, 4 days). The live endpoint keeps no archive, but the WRD department's dated Marathi copy does, from early 2024 (see playbook); backfill_pravah_marathi_archive.py reads it.

playbook: Run build_ingres_gwr.py --city nagpur first: this producer places stations in public/geojson/nagpur-gwr-blocks.geojson (properties.block) and exits 1 if none place.
Run build_nwdp_gw_stations.py --city nagpur. It pages about 400,000 rows (the GSDA 2021-2025 resource alone is about 299,000) at 32,000 per call, so it takes several minutes.

Read the printed summary against the last run (2026-10-15: 101 stations placed, 1 outside, Nagpur (Urban) 3, all CGWB). A fall in placed stations means a resource id or row shape changed, not that wells closed; probe the resource's fields and its distinct District values before trusting a count.

Freshness is per agency. On 2026-10-15 every CGWB station's last reading was 2026-06-02 to 2026-06-19 and the 20 National Hydrology Project GSDA stations stopped 31 May to 2 June 2026, while 62 Atal Bhujal stations reported raw readings into September 2026 (59 keep a September monthly mean after the quality rules). A station whose latest month stops advancing is an upstream pause; check the same station on India-WRIS before calling it a fault here.
The portal opens a new resource for each five-year block; the 2031-2035 resources will need adding to CITIES['nagpur'].resources.

GSDA's manual monthly resource bb185a88-c7c3-483f-b06e-784ce5322ff8 (two NMC dug wells, 1990-2025) has a different row shape (Well ID, District Name, Date of Monitoring dd-mm-YYYY, 'Water Level, m bgl' positive down). Do not add it to this producer; it needs its own adapter and its own layer.

Never average these wells (CGWB's ten piezometers in the district are semi-confined, 23.5 to 69.5 m deep per India-WRIS; 12 GSDA NHP stations are dug wells) into a ward or city depth; groundwaterViews.depth stays false.

sources.refreshMethod: manual: pdftotext -layout each river PDF, re-run the column-position parse into pipeline-inputs/nagpur/river-mpcb-monthly-2017-2024.csv (stations 2170, 2171, 1909, 1908, 1910 only), then python3 neer-vazhvu-api/scripts/build_nagpur_river_quality.py, which fails if the 2021-2024 months stop reproducing CPCB's yearly table
playbook: The page lists one PDF per polluted river ('Latest Water Quality As per Assessment Targeted'); Nagpur's are Kanhan river.pdf (2170, 2171, 1909), Kolar river.pdf (1908) and Wainganga River.pdf (1910 plus Bhandara and Chandrapur stations 11, 2172, 2173, 2175, 2176, which are not used). Drupal appends _0, _1 to a re-uploaded name, which is what this link-set sees; if a file is overwritten in place, compare sha256 with the INVENTORY line.

Each station block is 12 months x 8 years with the month label printed after the fourth year. Parse by column position, not token order: blank FC/TC cells occur (2170 and 2171 March 2018, 2170 September 2018, 1909 and 1910 July 2021 TC), and in Wainganga River.pdf the 1910 February 2021 values are printed on the line BELOW the year. Reading that wrapped line is what makes 1910's 2021 DO maximum (7.1) agree with CPCB.

'Dry' and 'Stagnant water' are verdicts in the bathing-criteria column with no values: carry the month as a reading with that condition and nulls, never as zero. 1909 Agargaon was dry every June 2019-2024; 1908 Waregaon May-August 2019.
FC can be printed '<1.8' (1909 August 2021): keep it as below detection, not as 1.8. CPCB's yearly table rounds the same month to 2.

Cross-check before shipping: for 2021-2024 the yearly min and max of the months equal CPCB's NWMP yearly table for DO and BOD exactly, FC after rounding. 2018 and 2019 do NOT agree (CPCB 2018 prints Kolar 1908 BOD max 60.0 where MPCB's months peak at 18.1): record the disagreement, never headline the CPCB 2018 figure.
The bathing-criteria verdict is blank for 2171 April-December 2024 and 1908 July 2024 as printed; leave it blank.
sources.notes: Monthly pH, DO, BOD, faecal and total coliform at every NWMP station on Maharashtra's polluted stretches, 2017-2024, the finest-grained public record for the Kanhan below Nagpur (it adds 2020, which CPCB's yearly file omits for Nagpur). PDFs created 2-5 May 2025; re-downloaded 15 Oct 2026 with identical bytes (Kanhan d0be402c, Kolar 450fa59c, Wainganga 830ad972).

sources.refreshMethod: manual: transcribe the new edition's river tables (6.13-6.16 in 2023-24) into pipeline-inputs/nagpur/river-nmc-esr-<edition>-sites.csv and Table 6.3 into river-stps-esr-<edition>.csv, point neer-vazhvu-api/scripts/build_nagpur_river_quality.py at them and rerun; it fails unless the operating plants sum to the text's treated figure
playbook: Printed page = PDF page - 1 in 2023-24. River tables: 6.13 sites and DMS coordinates (printed pp.161-162), 6.14 physico-chemical (pp.163-164), 6.15 coliforms (p.165), 6.16 DO, COD, TKN, phosphate (p.166). STPs: Table 6.3 (p.137); the sewage sentence (520 generated, 403.5 treated at 12 STPs) is on p.136.
There is no BOD column in the river tables. Do not derive one from COD.
Coliforms are CFU/100 ml, not MPN. Pilli-5 (FC 140,000 > TC 100,000) and Pilli-6 (FC 300,000 > TC 140,000) print more faecal than total coliforms: ship as printed with the note, do not swap.
EC is headed uS/cm but the values (0.464-0.854) are in the mS/cm range; nitrate is 'as N'. Neither is carried.
COD 'ND' at Nag-1 and Pora-2 is below detection, not zero. The text says the Nag starts at COD 30.95; Table 6.16 gives that value to Nag-2 and ND to Nag-1. The table is what ships.
The sampling season changes between editions (2023-24: monsoon, before the festive season; 2022-23: end of monsoon, after it). Do not chart editions against each other as a trend.
Pora-1 to Pora-4 have coordinates but no place names. Nag-7's printed description has an unbalanced parenthesis; place_as_printed keeps it.
Table 6.3 'utilisation' equals capacity on every row and 520 MLD is 73% of supply, not a measured flow; say so wherever either is shown. Narsala is 'WIP / Trial run' and is not in the 12.
The 2024-25 edition was reported tabled in April 2026 but was not online on 15 Oct 2026; check the public-notices page and NMC's Environment department page.
